elements.element: Mutual cap of 12 months' fees (fallback basis)
elements.evidence: limited to the greater of the value of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000 — a greater-of cap, not a bare 12 months' fees cap

elements.element: Fallback carve-outs: indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: either Party's indemnification obligations, breach of its confidentiality ... gross negligence, willful misconduct

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully satisfied: greater-of cap with the exact fee basis and claim anchor plus the USD 1,000,000 floor, mutual exclusion of indirect damages retained in (a), the full carve-out set (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP infringement) stated mutually, and payment obligations expressly excluded from 'damages'.
Fallback is read literally as a flat 12 months' fees cap, so the greater-of formulation does not satisfy that separate bargain; this is immaterial because the drafter targeted preferred.

Minimality holds: the cap basis sentence was replaced only to change the 3% bill-of-materials measure, and the carve-out sentence is a concise insertion for an absent provision. The short gloss 'being IBM's obligation to pay all amounts due under this Agreement' is arguably necessary because 'Customer' is not a defined party here (the Agreement uses IBM/MSL and separately 'IBM Customers'), so it avoids an undefined term rather than adding new protection; 'the value of' is a harmless carryover from the original wording.
Intent preserved: paragraph (a)'s consequential-damages exclusion and all untouched terms remain effective; no contradiction or dangling mechanic is introduced.
